extracted.intended_audience: researchers and engineers developing or evaluating LLMs for patent concept/text generation and patent practitioners interested in AI-assisted drafting
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, fine-tuning, and evaluating large language models to autonomously mine domain knowledge and generate initial patent concepts and patent text (titles, abstracts, claims) using a Knowledge Fine-Tuning (KFT) workflow. Includes data curation (USPTO corpora, knowledge graphs), SFT, RLHF, and multiple automated and human-centered evaluation benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge Fine-Tuning (KFT) workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: A workflow that enhances LLM performance in concepts and patents generation by incorporating knowledge injection pre-training (KPT), domain-specific supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KFT combines structured knowledge and original text: (1) Knowledge Injection (transform structured triples into text and inject during pre-training), (2) SFT with domain-specific datasets (fine-tune on patent drafting dialogues), and (3) RLHF (align outputs with human knowledge recognition). The paper claims KFT significantly improves downstream patent-writing performance compared to traditional PT + SFT + RLHF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge extracting (KG construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatically extract concept entities and relationships from patent text to build a knowledge graph K with triples (h, r, t) using prompts and an LLM extractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: input general corpus G (USPTO patent texts), use LLM πθ with prompts (Appendix A) to produce triplets Ti = argmax(h,r,t) πθ(h,r,t | gi), aggregate Ti across corpus to obtain K. Intended entity/relation classification follows predefined entity and relation types (see Table 2 & Table 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge injecting (convert triples to natural text and pre-train)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform each structured triple in the extracted knowledge graph into natural language sentences si and use these to form a knowledge corpus S for continued pre-training (knowledge injection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion uses a prompt (Appendix B). Continued pre-training loss LPT = α E_s∈S[log πχ(y|s)] + β E_g∈G[log πχ(y|g)], where α and β weight importance of knowledge corpus S and general corpus G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge learning (Supervised Fine-Tuning, SFT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Align model outputs to specific patent drafting tasks by training on a dialogue dataset Q of (q, a) pairs to reduce differences between outputs and ground-truth labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SFT loss LSFT(χ) = E(q,a)∈Q[log πχ(a|q)]. The SFT dialogue dataset in the paper contains 60,000 Q–A pairs for drafting patent titles, abstracts, and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge feedbacking (RLHF with human preference data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refine model outputs through Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: collect preference-labeled interactions H = {(q, p, n)}, train a reward model to predict human preferences, and apply PPO to fine-tune the LLM using the reward signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward model loss LRM = E(q,p,n)∈H[log σ(rρ(p|q) - rρ(n|q))]. PPO objective LPPO = E[min(r_t(χ)A_t, clip(r_t(χ),1-ε,1+ε)A_t)] with r_t(χ)=πχ(a|q)/πχ_old(a|q). Human feedback dataset described: 2,000 interactions with preferred/non-preferred answers annotated by experienced patent practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO patent text dataset composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-training corpus sourced from USPTO patents published between 2021 and 2022, sampled by IPC to ensure industry balance; includes patent titles, abstracts, and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 20,000 patents collected, with each of the eight IPC sections containing between 2,000 and 4,000 patents to ensure balanced representation across fields A–H. Used for continued pre-training and for building KG and SFT datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Knowledge Graph (KG) dataset construction criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: KG built from a subset (30%) of USPTO Patent Text Dataset using LLM extraction prompts; resulting KG contains entities and relationships represented as triples (~100,000 entities, ~300,000 relations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities and relationships are identified/classified strictly according to predefined types (see Table 2 entity types and Table 3 relation types). Triples are converted into natural language descriptions for knowledge injecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: SFT dialogue dataset requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogues for supervised fine-tuning should reflect patent drafting scenarios (titles, abstracts, claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper's SFT dataset contains 60,000 question–answer pairs derived from USPTO patent texts; dataset design should capture drafting tasks to teach the model how to use injected knowledge in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human feedback dataset annotation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Human preference annotations used to train the reward model must be provided by experienced patent practitioners to ensure legal and technical quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each query includes two candidate answers (preferred and non-preferred); annotations prioritize answers consistent with human knowledge recognition and legal accuracy. The paper used 2,000 such annotated interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUGE-1
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures overlap between generated text and the 1-gram in the reference text, emphasizing word-level coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formula provided: ROUGE-1 = (sum_{w∈Ref} Count1-gram(w)) / (sum_{w∈Ref} Count(w)). Useful to assess word-level coverage vs. reference patent texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUGE-2
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures overlap between generated text and the 2-gram in the reference text, capturing phrase-level matches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formula provided analogous to ROUGE-1 but for 2-grams. Useful for assessing short-phrase fidelity to reference patent text.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUGE-L
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on longest common subsequence (LCS) to calculate F-measure, reflecting similarity in semantic order and structure between generated and reference text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulas for RLCS, PLCS, FLCS provided using LCS(X,Y), lengths m and n, and β to trade precision/recall. Useful for structural similarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: BLEU-4
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures n-gram precision (up to 4-grams) with a length penalty to reflect syntactic accuracy and fluency of generated text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BLEU formula with brevity penalty BP is provided. BLEU-4 is used in the paper to reflect accuracy of phrase matching in generated patent text (paper reports BLEU-4 as an important indicator of syntactic precision).

rubrics_metrics.name: BERTScore
rubrics_metrics.description: A semantic similarity-based evaluation using pre-trained language model embeddings to compute cosine similarity between generated and reference words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formula: average over generated tokens of max cosine(E(ti), E(rj)). Used to measure semantic match and domain-terminology understanding (paper reports BERTScore as a primary indicator of patent-writing quality).

rubrics_metrics.name: IP_Quiz
rubrics_metrics.description: A public dataset benchmark designed to evaluate a model’s understanding of IP concepts and regulations via multiple-choice questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model must select the correct answer from candidates; number of correct selections indicates proficiency in IP concept comprehension (sourced from prior benchmark work [25]).

rubrics_metrics.name: IP_Match
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark to evaluate whether the model understands the invention described in a patent and can accurately distinguish different patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess document-level comprehension and patent-distinction capability (from public benchmark on Hugging Face).

rubrics_metrics.name: IP_Exam (Patent Bar style multiple-choice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Custom benchmark derived from multiple-choice Q&A content used in the U.S. Patent Bar Examination to assess knowledge of IP law principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher performance indicates capability to understand and apply IP law principles; used to evaluate legal-awareness of the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding)
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad benchmark assessing model performance across many tasks and disciplines to gauge general language understanding and robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher MMLU scores reflect versatility; included to show model's general capabilities beyond IP domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent writing benchmark (task sampling and prompt design)
rubrics_metrics.description: A benchmark specifically evaluating LLMs' ability to write patentable concept texts: 1,000 instances sampled from all eight IPC categories using a designed prompt (Appendix C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates title/abstract/claim generation quality across diverse fields; ensures sampling across IPC for coverage of industry domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept Generation Evaluation — Reasonability (USPTO standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human/LLM judging whether generated initial concept texts meet the reasonability of patent application and conform to USPTO standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper used ChatGPT-4 as a judge on 100 randomly selected samples to determine whether generated texts meet reasonability; intended as an automated proxy but recognizes need for legal expert validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept Generation Evaluation — Innovation (novelty/uniqueness via TechNet)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure innovation of generated patent text by analyzing novelty and uniqueness relative to existing patent databases using TechNet's evaluation method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied after filtering for 'reasonable' texts (USPTO-conforming); higher innovation scores indicate greater novelty relative to patent corpus; paper also uses a rarity/novelty score but notes this is not a substitute for legal patentability analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty, legal compliance, and plagiarism risk check
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative assessment required to evaluate originality, sufficiency of disclosure, compliance with patent laws across jurisdictions, and risk of unintentional plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors caution that automated rarity/novelty scores do not replace legal assessment by patent attorneys; future work should integrate legal expert evaluations to assess patentability and compliance systematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hallucination and domain-coverage risk (applicability to emerging domains)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of model reliability in emerging technical domains (quantum computing, BCI, synthetic biology) where training data may be insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper notes PatentGPT (trained on patents 2021–2022) may hallucinate or generate technically inaccurate claims in underrepresented or emerging fields; recommends integrating external retrieval or continuous knowledge updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with human knowledge recognition (RLHF success criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which RLHF-refined outputs align with human preferences and knowledge recognition as measured by reward-model-guided PPO finetuning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured indirectly via downstream evaluation improvements (KPT + SFT + RLHF achieved highest BERTScore and BLEU-4). Requires high-quality human preference annotations by domain experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical & misuse risk assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of potential misuse risks (e.g., enabling excessive/low-quality patent filings, raising barriers for smaller entities) and ethical implications of AI-assisted patent generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors recommend AI auditing frameworks and engagement with patent offices/policymakers to mitigate misuse and study broader IP system impacts. This is a societal-level evaluation criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: KG entity type taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Entity categories used in the KG: Task/Method, Material, Generic, Definition (and examples in Table 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines what entity types the extraction model should identify: e.g., Applications/problems to solve (Task), Methods/models/systems (Method), Data/datasets/resources (Material), and General terms/pronouns (Generic). Adherence ensures KG consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: KG relation type taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Relation categories used in the KG: Used-for, Feature-of, Hyponym-of, Part-of, Compare, Conjunction (Table 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each relation has a definition (e.g., Used-for: B is used for A; Feature-of: B belongs to A). Relation typing guides correct triple extraction and downstream conversion into natural language training data.
